summary:
New A2 direction on runtime configuration authority, with a decisive probe submitted (valid:true).

Source reading:
`ReloadConfig` merges exactly the five reloadable fields (TrailingLogs, SnapshotInterval, SnapshotThreshold, HeartbeatTimeout, ElectionTimeout) onto the current configuration under a reload lock, runs the same validation the constructor uses on the merged result, and stores it only when validation succeeds (api.go:713-741, config.go:267-313); a successful reload that lowers the heartbeat additionally notifies the leader and follower channels so replication and heartbeat timers adopt the shorter value. Fields outside that set, such as the leader lease, are not reloadable and are taken from the current configuration when the merged result is validated.

Probe (draft/assurance_reload_config.go): a single-node cluster reads `ReloadableConfig`, attempts an invalid reload that lowers heartbeat and election to 10ms while the non-reloadable lease stays at 50ms, then attempts a valid reload raising both to 100ms, emitting the returned error, whether the reported configuration is unchanged, and whether the new value was applied.

Comparisons requested (all admitted 1:1 on the single probe-start event, so no correlation ambiguity): the invalid merged configuration is rejected (error not empty); the rejected reload leaves the running configuration unchanged; and — as control — the valid reload is accepted and visible through `ReloadableConfig`, with applicability limited to the successful case. A requirement and responsibility were declared with an anchor at `Raft.ReloadConfig`, plus the already-recorded lease-versus-heartbeat validation source.

Native local run, flagged in the limitations as non-retained evidence: heartbeat/election 50ms and lease 50ms before; the invalid reload failed with "LeaderLeaseTimeout (50ms) cannot be larger than heartbeat timeout (10ms)" with `config_unchanged` true; the valid reload to 100ms was accepted and reported, lease still 50ms. So the probe finds no defect here — a running node cannot be put into a state its constructor would reject — and the controller's execution will decide the three comparisons formally.
